title: managed
description:
The wire contract for the managed-agent port: one provider-neutral description of a graded, sandboxed, tool-using model session, the handle to one in flight, and the observations and evidence it produces.

This document is the source of truth. The Go types in types.gen.go are generated from it, and a port to another language generates from the same file. What the document cannot state is the part that matters most — usage is a cumulative total, state moves forwards only, evidence is readable until release — so read it alongside the rules in the README.

RuntimeName.description: RuntimeName identifies one runtime adapter — the thing that executes a session, which is not the same as the vendor that bills for the model it uses. Every durable reference carries one, so the name must be canonical for a persisted session to route back to the adapter that started it.

Meter.description: Meter names a billable quantity that is not a token bucket, such as a container second or a hosted tool call. The set is open because each runtime emits its own, but a meter must be priced before a session using it can settle.

x-go-consts.title: MeterChargedCost
x-go-consts.description: MeterChargedCost is the micro-USD a runtime's own platform has already charged someone for the session, such as a platform charging the person who started it. It is reported, never priced: a rate card that priced it would charge the same money a second time.

NetworkMode.description: NetworkMode is the outbound network policy a sandbox runs under. The empty value is not a mode: validation reads an omitted mode as none, so a specification that forgets to say gets the closed sandbox rather than the open one.

oneOf.title: NetworkNone
oneOf.description: NetworkNone closes the sandbox off. It may carry neither domains nor secrets.

oneOf.title: NetworkAllowlist
oneOf.description: NetworkAllowlist permits the named domains and nothing else. It is the only mode that may carry secrets, and each one is bound to a domain the allowlist names.

oneOf.title: NetworkOpen
oneOf.description: NetworkOpen lifts every restriction. It may carry neither domains nor host-bound secrets, because there is no host binding left to enforce.

AccessMode.description: AccessMode is how a session may use a mounted repository. Runtimes advertise the modes they honor in Capabilities, so a specification asking for more than the runtime allows is refused before the session starts.

oneOf.title: AccessReadOnly
oneOf.description: AccessReadOnly states that the session must not write to the repository. The enforcement is the credential's own scope; the mode tells the runtime what to arrange.

oneOf.title: AccessReadWrite
oneOf.description: AccessReadWrite obliges the specification to name a credential reference, since a mount the session can push to needs one.

ResourceKind.description: ResourceKind says which payload of a Resource is the live one. Exactly one payload may be set and it must be the one the kind names; validation rejects the mismatch rather than guessing.

oneOf.title: ResourceAttachment
oneOf.description: ResourceAttachment carries file content inline with a SHA-256 the validator recomputes.

oneOf.title: ResourceRepository
oneOf.description: ResourceRepository names an HTTPS repository to place at a destination inside the workspace.

oneOf.title: ResourceInput
oneOf.description: ResourceInput carries a file the session reads and may not change, placed outside the workspace under Capabilities.InputDir.

TerminalReason.description: TerminalReason says why a session stopped, and is carried only on a terminal Status. A failed state alone cannot tell a run the runtime broke on from one that was cancelled or timed out, and operators chase those in different places.

oneOf.title: ReasonSucceeded
oneOf.description: ReasonSucceeded is the work finishing on its own terms.

oneOf.title: ReasonEvaluationFailed
oneOf.description: ReasonEvaluationFailed is the work finishing and the evaluator deciding against it.

oneOf.title: ReasonCancelled
oneOf.description: ReasonCancelled is a session stopped from outside.

oneOf.title: ReasonTimedOut
oneOf.description: ReasonTimedOut is a session that stopped answering rather than one that failed. The distinction is the point: a fault the runtime owned up to and a runtime that went quiet are chased in different places.

oneOf.title: ReasonRuntimeFailed
oneOf.description: ReasonRuntimeFailed is a fault the runtime reported.

oneOf.title: ReasonPolicyRefused
oneOf.description: ReasonPolicyRefused is a session a runtime declined on policy grounds rather than ran, without the work ever starting.

Role.description: Role is who a transcript event is attributed to. The set is closed: an adapter maps every runtime-native speaker onto one of these.

oneOf.title: RoleUser
oneOf.description: RoleUser is the caller the model answers.

oneOf.title: RoleSystem
oneOf.description: RoleSystem is the harness around them both.

EventKind.description: EventKind is what a transcript event is. Unlike Role the set is deliberately open: the kinds below are named so callers compare against a constant rather than a bare string, while a runtime-native kind passes through unchanged rather than being dropped or coerced into a neighbor.

x-go-consts.title: KindMessage
x-go-consts.description: KindMessage is text from one of the roles.

x-go-consts.title: KindThinking
x-go-consts.description: KindThinking is reasoning the model exposed.

x-go-consts.title: KindToolUse
x-go-consts.description: KindToolUse is the model calling a tool.

x-go-consts.title: KindToolResult
x-go-consts.description: KindToolResult is what the tool answered.

ModelRef.description: ModelRef is the exact, provider-qualified model a session ran on, and the key a rate card is resolved against. Provider is the inference and cost source rather than the runtime, so a session may run on one runtime and bill against another vendor's model. BillingVariant records a price-affecting applied class such as a service tier, and stays empty where the provider has one price.

ModelSelector.description: ModelSelector is how a specification asks for a model. Exactly one form is set: a preference tier the runtime resolves for itself (best, balanced, fast), or one exact reference the caller insists on. Either way the runtime reports the model it actually resolved in Status, so a record of what ran never depends on the tier being re-resolved later.

Model.description: Model is one model a runtime offers, with the preference tiers it can serve. Tier resolution matches a requested preference against Preferences, so one reference may answer to several tiers where a runtime offers only one model.

Package.description: Package is one dependency installed into the sandbox before the session runs. Manager is drawn from the set an adapter declares it supports: a manager the adapter cannot install fails validation rather than being skipped so the session runs without its dependency. An empty Version leaves the choice to the manager.

NetworkPolicy.description: NetworkPolicy is the sandbox's egress rule. Mode governs the other two fields: none rejects both, allowlist requires at least one domain, and open refuses host-bound secrets. SecretRefs maps an environment variable name to a "domain:name" reference whose domain must itself be allowlisted; a specification carries references only, never secret values.

SandboxSpec.description: SandboxSpec is the machine the work happens on, stated explicitly so an adapter can refuse what it cannot provide before anything remote is created. Bootstrap entries are argv arrays rather than shell fragments, so nothing in a specification is handed to a shell to interpret.

AttachmentResource.description:
AttachmentResource is one file placed into the sandbox outside any mounted repository — an input the session must read but must not commit. SHA256 is verified against Content during validation, so a corrupted or substituted payload fails the specification instead of the run.

Keeping attachments outside every repository destination is structural rather than stylistic: it is what makes "this data is not ours to redistribute" enforceable by the filesystem layout, not by the model's good behavior.

InputResource.description: InputResource is a file the session reads and may not change, such as the one copy of a paper every run of a study is given. The runtime places it at Path under Capabilities.InputDir, outside the workspace, and makes it read-only, so the agent can neither edit it nor commit it into what the session produces. SHA256 is verified against Content during validation, as for an attachment, and is what a run's record cites as the input it was given.

RepositoryResource.description:
RepositoryResource is a version-control repository the session works in. A runtime may mount it, clone it, or stage it some other way, as long as the resulting filesystem and write authority match Access. CredentialRef names a credential and never carries one; read-write access requires it, because an unauthenticated write mount would fail only once the session was already running.

AccessReadOnly states intent. The enforcement is the credential's own scope, so a read-only destination must be given a read-only credential: the field tells the runtime what to arrange, it does not by itself prevent a push.

Resource.description: Resource is the tagged union of things a session can be given. Kind selects which payload is set, and exactly one must be. An unknown kind fails validation rather than being ignored, so a session never runs quietly missing an input the caller asked for.

EvaluationSpec.description:
EvaluationSpec makes a session graded. An absent EvaluationSpec on SessionSpec is the only way to say "ungraded", which is why a present one must carry a non-empty rubric: a zero value must not be readable as grading against nothing. MaxRevisions may be zero, which grades the first attempt and never revises it, so a study can keep what a run produced before a rubric pushed it.

Findings names the workspace file that holds the run's findings as data. A runtime that declares FindingsRounds keeps it after every worker-side stage, checks it, and gives the problems to the grader and to the revision, so a file the system cannot read is never passed on a model's reading of the rubric. Empty asks for none of this.

SessionSpec.description: SessionSpec is the complete intent for one session, independent of the runtime that will execute it. Instructions is the worker's durable role and Task is this session's request; an adapter with no persistent worker may combine the two on the wire, but may not reorder them or change what they mean.

SessionRef.description:
SessionRef is the handle to a session: everything needed to poll it, read its evidence, cancel it, and release it. Runtime and ID are fixed for the session's life and Revision only ever increases, so a checkpoint can be persisted with compare-and-swap.

How long the handle stays meaningful is the runtime's to declare, not this contract's to promise. A runtime reporting Capabilities.Resumable may be handed a reference reconstructed in a later process and will still find the session; one reporting false will not, and the reference is good only inside the process that started the session. A caller that must survive a restart checks the capability at admission rather than discovering the difference when a restart happens.

Locator is adapter-owned recovery metadata that a caller stores and returns byte for byte but never parses; LocatorVersion versions its shape, and it is size-limited and forbidden from carrying credentials or user content.

Verdict.description: Verdict is the evaluator's decision about a graded session. Explanation is the reasoning a reader is shown alongside the grade; a runtime that gives none leaves it empty rather than inventing one.

Usage.description:
Usage is the cumulative, provider-neutral cost of a session so far. The six token buckets are mutually exclusive so each is priced exactly once; Extra holds billable non-token meters, and Details holds non-billable decomposition such as reasoning tokens already counted in Output, which pricing never iterates. Anything the runtime did not report is zero, never an estimate dressed up as provider data.

Usage is a running total for the whole session, not a delta for one call. A caller accumulates observations by replacement, so a runtime reporting deltas would be billed several times over; ValidateObservation refuses a total that decreased for exactly that reason.

input_fresh.description: InputFresh is prompt tokens the provider processed from scratch.

input_cached.description: InputCached is prompt tokens served from the provider's cache rather than processed fresh. It is priced far below InputFresh, which is why it is a bucket of its own rather than folded into it.

cache_write.description: CacheWrite is cache-write tokens whose bought lifetime the runtime did not report. It is kept separate from the two known lifetimes so that "we do not know which" stays visible rather than being guessed into a cheaper bucket.

cache_write_5m.description: CacheWrite5m is cache-write tokens that bought the shorter cache lifetime.

cache_write_1h.description: CacheWrite1h is cache-write tokens that bought the longer cache lifetime. It costs more than the shorter one, so folding the two together loses money in one direction and overcharges in the other.

output.description: Output is tokens the model produced.

extra.description: Extra holds billable non-token meters, such as a container second or a hosted tool call.

details.description: Details holds non-billable decomposition of the buckets above, such as reasoning tokens already counted in Output. Pricing never iterates it, so a new entry here can never change a bill.

Status.description: Status is one observation of a session: where it has got to, what it has cost so far, and once terminal, why it stopped. Between observations only the reference's Revision and Locator may advance, state moves forwards only, and a terminal observation stays terminal however often the session is polled. An ungraded session finishes with no Verdict at all; a graded one may not finish without a decided verdict.

Event.description: Event is one entry in a session's transcript, normalized across runtimes. ID is stable, so re-reading the transcript neither duplicates entries nor changes what an existing one means. Raw keeps the runtime's own payload intact, because the transcript is the evidence for a run and must not be reduced to this contract's vocabulary.

Artifact.description: Artifact is one file the session produced. Path is a clean, relative, slash-separated path, unique within the session, and is what a reader sees; ID is the runtime's own handle for the same file and is passed back when fetching it, since not every backend addresses a file by path.

Capabilities.description: Capabilities is what a runtime can actually do, stated as semantic flags and limits rather than vendor product names. It exists so a specification is refused before anything remote is created: there is no best-effort mode in which an unsupported package manager, network mode, or oversized attachment is silently dropped.

output_dir.description: OutputDir is the sandbox path a session is told to write its artifacts to. A caller templates it into the instructions rather than hard-coding one backend's filesystem layout.

input_dir.description: InputDir is the sandbox path inputs are placed under, outside the workspace. Empty means the runtime cannot hand a session a file it can read and not change, and a specification carrying an input is refused.

package_managers.description: PackageManagers are the managers this runtime can install from, keyed by the name a Package carries.

network_modes.description: NetworkModes are the egress policies this runtime can impose. A mode absent here is refused, never downgraded to a stricter one that happens to be supported.

repository_modes.description: RepositoryModes are the repository access modes this runtime can arrange.

evaluation.description: Evaluation reports whether this runtime can grade a session against a rubric. When false, a specification carrying an EvaluationSpec is refused: grading is not something a caller can bolt on afterwards from a transcript.

durable_events.description: DurableEvents reports whether the transcript is stored by the runtime rather than buffered in this process. When false the evidence dies with the process, so a caller that wants to keep it must read it before letting the process end.

artifacts.description: Artifacts reports whether the runtime can enumerate the files a session produced. When false, ListArtifacts refuses rather than returning an empty list, which would read as "the session produced nothing".

cancellation.description: Cancellation reports whether a running session can be stopped. When false, Cancel refuses and a caller's only lever is to stop reading.

resumable.description:
Resumable reports whether a SessionRef survives the process that created it. When true, a reference persisted now can be handed back to a fresh process later and will still name a live session. When false the reference is meaningful only inside the process that started the session: an adapter over an in-process runtime declares false, and a caller that must survive a restart refuses the runtime at admission rather than discovering the loss when a restart happens.

This is separate from DurableEvents on purpose. That flag is about the evidence outliving the process; this one is about the handle doing so. A runtime can lose one and keep the other.

max_attachment_bytes.description: MaxAttachmentBytes bounds one attachment's content. Zero means the runtime declares no bound.

max_locator_bytes.description: MaxLocatorBytes bounds the locator this runtime writes into a reference. Zero means DefaultMaxLocatorBytes.

findings_rounds.description: FindingsRounds reports that the runtime keeps the findings file of every grading round and checks it before the grader reads it, which an EvaluationSpec asks for by naming Findings. A runtime that grades on a vendor's side cannot reach inside that loop and declares false.
